notes: encoding::gob follows Go's gob byte for byte: type ids (predefined 1..23, user ids from 64 in first-sent order), wire types, field-number deltas, zero omission, pointer flattening, interface values by registered name with inline type definitions, GobEncoder/BinaryMarshaler types, and the decoder's compile step (compatibility checks, ignored fields, overflow and corrupt-data error texts, including Go's behaviour of reading type ids). Values come from rust_stdlib::reflect, so any #[derive(Reflect)] type works. Verified by tools/gob_check.py, a differential against Go over generated typed values (equal bytes, cross-decoding, merges, schema evolution, corrupted streams). Rust-shaped differences: Encode and Decode take any Reflect type (Decode copies in and out through reflect::edit); Decode(nil) is decode_discard; errors are std::io::Error with the io sentinels for EOF; a GobEncoder or BinaryMarshaler is a type with #[reflect_methods] methods of those Go names; a Rust map built from a Rust value is never nil, so an empty map field is sent where Go omits a nil map (values built with reflect::zero/new keep Go's nil maps).

Decoder.Decode.note: generic over Reflect types; Decode(nil) is Decoder::decode_discard

Encoder.Encode.note: a map built from a Rust value is never nil, so an empty map field is sent where Go omits a nil map; reflect values keep nil maps

NewDecoder.note: buffers the reader; Decoder::from_byte_reader is Go's unwrapped io.ByteReader case

Register.note: register_value takes a reflect::Value; a pointer type is an Option
